production.candidate_status: Owner promotion decided 2026-11-08; confirmatory held-out running (internal tables + paired seeded JSettlers). PASS confirms the promotion, FAIL keeps planner_offer_accept.

current_rules: Every run is seeded and predeclared with a numeric bar and a power block before any game; a failed bar is a result and is not retuned.

Internal tables are paired: each seed is played with the candidate rotated through all four seats and again with the control in the same seats and dice. Tables: tactical (3 Tactical), mixed (Builder, Tactical, Expander), self (3 copies of the served bot).
Promotion path in PLAN.md: +5 pp on every table in a DEV screen earns a held-out run; a held-out pass (LCB > 0 on every table) supports promotion; promotion is the owner's call.

External ladders: one bot vs three copies of an outside AI, rotated through every seat; fair share .25. Retirement rule: retire an outside AI as a benchmark for a bot once that bot wins >= .50 with the 95% lower bound > .40.
evaluation.owner_direction: Evaluate candidates by screens against our best policies and the best external policies (Jerry 2026-11-08).
open_questions: Which internal comparator: the served bot or our strongest candidate? (Recent screens use the strongest candidate, e.g. +.02 over planner_pv2_tiles.)
JSettlers as a required table: added (as in the held-out) or replacing the internal tables? Paired seeded JSettlers became possible with the seed patch (#40).
STAC POMCP-TS-CR as the strongest external opponent: benchmark design (seat rotation, soft time cap) after the bridge review (#41).
Metric: wins per paired round stay the decision metric; final-VP margin is about as sensitive and may be reported as a secondary.
Bar size: the transformer's true Tactical/mixed lift (~+4.5) sits just under +5, so a +5 DEV screen is close to a coin flip for it.

models.note: Offline gate, then +.02 screen vs planner_pv2_tiles.

findings: Build/trade decisions: a 32-playout selector gains under 1 pp per decision over the served move (label reliability .23 to .30).
Opening placement: +.105 [+.035, +.180] per decision vs Tactical (reliability .82); robber and trade answers show no headroom.
Search gains follow the opponent model the playouts assume.
Tile tokens beat flat features and a hex CNN offline; every value model over-ranks 'build a city' against 'end the turn' (.92 vs .56 in playouts).
STAC's POMCP spends ~0.8 s and 10k simulations per decision; our bots look one turn ahead in milliseconds. Deeper search (PUCT) is the next lever.

policies.name: planner_offer_accept
policies.search: One-turn build search over builds, bank trades and cards, plus one priced trade offer per turn
policies.model: Fitted economic score (hand-built features, fitted weights)
policies.note: Production since 2026-11-03. STAC is an 8-game smoke, not a benchmark.

policies.name: planner_pv2_tiles

policies.note: Owner promotion; confirmatory held-out running. Catanatron retired for this bot.

policies.note: Screen is vs planner_pv2_tiles (+2 pp every table). Pre-screen: 100 simulations/decision, principal lines ~4.5 turns deep.
